name: RMOL (Revenue Management Open Library)
what_it_holds: C++ open-source revenue-management simulation library (part of the airsim/travel-market-simulator suite alongside stdair, airinv, tvlsim). Implements classic RM optimisation (EMSR, nesting, forecasting of booking curves) originally built for airline seat inventory but generically applicable to any capacity/date-based booking-curve RM problem, including hotel rooms. No committed real-world hotel data; it is a simulator/library, not a dataset.
why_useful: Could be used to synthesize realistic booking-curve / lead-time / cancellation-and-no-show test data under controllable demand assumptions as a kernel analogue for RNPL/booking-pace modeling (gap #17 methods, gap #18 book-ahead analogues), though it requires nontrivial setup and produces simulated, not observed, data.
license: Open source (LGPL per airsim project convention)
last_activity: Low-activity legacy academic project (airsim org, 14 stars)
themes: Hotel booking demand datasets (Antonio Almeida Nunes and successors), hotel PMS datasets, revenue-management datasets with cancellations and lead times
why_all: Could be used to synthesize realistic booking-curve / lead-time / cancellation-and-no-show test data under controllable demand assumptions as a kernel analogue for RNPL/booking-pace modeling (gap #17 methods, gap #18 book-ahead analogues), though it requires nontrivial setup and produces simulated, not observed, data.

name: opentravel-alliance (API Evangelist profile)
what_it_holds: Profile of the OpenTravel Alliance standards body covering air/hospitality/car-rental/cruise/rail/GDS message specifications. Contains 8 harvested Swagger/OpenAPI docs and points to the upstream mirror github.com/OpenTravel/OpenTravel-Specifications, which the profile says holds 543 JSON Schema files (public OTA 1.0 tree stops at release 2017B; website offers releases through 2024A). No license file on this profiling repo. Last commit 2026-07-28 (creation); upstream mirror last updated 2024-11-26.
why_useful: Points to a real, larger upstream repo (OpenTravel/OpenTravel-Specifications) that defines the standard XML/JSON message formats used for cruise GDS booking/availability messages — a methods reference for anyone building a cruise-booking-API client, though not itself a dataset.
time_coverage: OTA 1.0 through 2017B (public mirror); commercial releases through 2024A not mirrored
license: royalty-free per OpenTravel Alliance (this profile repo has no LICENSE)
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Points to a real, larger upstream repo (OpenTravel/OpenTravel-Specifications) that defines the standard XML/JSON message formats used for cruise GDS booking/availability messages — a methods reference for anyone building a cruise-booking-API client, though not itself a dataset.

name: pyais
what_it_holds: Python library (254 stars) decoding AIS message formats (AIVDM/AIVDO) into vessel identification and position data. A decoder/parser only, no committed vessel data.
why_useful: Baseline tooling if the team ever wanted to build its own cruise-ship-position/port-call tracker from a raw AIS feed (e.g. AISHub free feed) rather than relying on a commercial API; general infrastructure only, several steps removed from any ABNB-relevant series today.
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
why_all: Baseline tooling if the team ever wanted to build its own cruise-ship-position/port-call tracker from a raw AIS feed (e.g. AISHub free feed) rather than relying on a commercial API; general infrastructure only, several steps removed from any ABNB-relevant series today.

name: onthebay98/tsa-forecast
what_it_holds: SARIMAX state-space probabilistic forecasting method for TSA checkpoint volumes; backtest window 2024-01-01 to 2026-02-22 (112+ weeks). NOTE: raw source code and data have been stripped from the public repo ("documentation only... actively deployed in production"); only ACF/forecast-error plot images remain in /data.
why_useful: Method-only reference (a public backtest window and SARIMAX framing for TSA nowcasting) but no runnable code or data — low value, flag mainly to avoid re-discovery.
duplicate_of_holding: Our own TSA-since-2024 nowcast attempt already failed; this is an independent method with no reusable artifact
themes: US air travel: BTS T-100 segment, DB1B fares, Form 41, on-time performance; repos that download and tidy them; TSA throughput scrapers
why_all: Method-only reference (a public backtest window and SARIMAX framing for TSA nowcasting) but no runnable code or data — low value, flag mainly to avoid re-discovery.

name: Covid-19-and-Aviation-Industry
what_it_holds: Spark/Airflow/AWS EMR pipeline (MIT, 29 commits) that pulls the OpenSky Network's post-2019-01-01 global flight dataset (2,500+ ADS-B receivers), joins it to JHU CSSE COVID-19 case time series, airport-code and country/continent mapping tables, and Indian state ISO codes, loading incrementally to S3.
why_useful: A concrete, working example of how to acquire and process the OpenSky COVID-19 global flight dataset at scale (see the top OpenSky COVID-19 entry above) -- useful as a reference implementation rather than a data source in itself.
duplicate_of_holding: companion method for the OpenSky COVID-19 dataset entry above
geography: global, with an India-specific join table
themes: Flight tracking and schedules: OpenSky, ADS-B Exchange, FlightRadar scrapers, aviationstack samples, airline seat capacity by route
why_all: A concrete, working example of how to acquire and process the OpenSky COVID-19 global flight dataset at scale (see the top OpenSky COVID-19 entry above) -- useful as a reference implementation rather than a data source in itself.
